name: Enhancing Research Capabilities in East Africa

content.title: Enhancing Research Capabilities in East Africa
content.summary: The Aga Khan University recently conducted a first-of-its-kind knowledge synthesis workshop in Nairobi, Kenya.

media.alt: Enhancing Research Capabilities in East Africa

content.text: The Aga Khan University recently conducted a first-of-its-kind knowledge synthesis workshop in Nairobi, Kenya. The three-day workshop was the result of an initiative - led by Division of Women and Child Health, AKU - with the aim of introducing evidence synthesis at the Nairobi campus. The workshop was conducted by Dr Jai Das and Ms Rehana Salam, senior instructors at AKU, and facilitated by Anthony Ngugi, Faculty Epidemiologist at the Nairobi campus.

Knowledge synthesis which combines information from research with that from policymakers in a systematic manner to make better use of knowledge by health care providers and institutions as well disease prevention institutions, health insurers and policymakers is much needed in East Africa given the paradox that large quantities of health research is available but poor health indicators bar researchers to come up with effective solutions to be implemented locally. "This is partially due to limited capacity for synthesis and translation into evidence-based health policies. Hence the need to conduct this workshop," said Salam.

The workshop was attended by 17 faculty and staff representing different areas such as  medicine, nursing, pharmacy and education. The workshop's interactive format was meant to introduce a step by step approach to evidence based systematic reviews.  After an initial introduction and explanation of the process involved, participants were asked to identify literature which could be used for a systematic review. Participants were briefed on how to conduct quality assessment of the findings avoiding risks of any biases; how to summarise the evidence and finally how to interpret them. Participants were also trained on using the meta-analysis software Revman independently.

"The participants are now equipped with the skills to enable them to search and synthesize relevant literature, not only for systematic reviews but also broadly for background literature review for their research proposals and manuscripts," said Ngugi elaborating on the outcomes of the workshop.

This workshop was also the first step towards the development of a knowledge synthesis and translation working group in AKU EA that would form an academic and research resource for the faculty of health sciences based in Nairobi. "This inaugural workshop of knowledge synthesis at Nairobi, Kenya is a vital step towards enhancing the research capacity and building knowledge translation platform," said Dr Das. "I hope this would motivate clinicians/scientists from all over Kenya to adopt this research approach and also would help build collaboration among various AKU entities."

"The success of this workshop is an important milestone in our efforts to develop research capacity among AKU faculty in Nairobi," said Ngugi. It would give not only a chance for post graduate trainees to opt for systematic review for their dissertation research, but develop knowledge synthesis skills among the faculty interested in research.
